Subject: SIG questionnaire: data retention & training clarifications

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking our SIG intake. We reviewed the spreadsheet you sent earlier and have a couple of follow-ups specifically around data handling and training policies before procurement can proceed:

1) Prompt/log retention: for API calls that contain PHI, what is your default retention window for raw requests and generated outputs? Is there an option for zero retention or immediate deletion?

2) Use of customer data for model training: do you ever use customer prompts or outputs to train models? If so, what opt-in/opt-out controls do customers have and how is that documented?

3) Evidence: can you provide any artifacts (SOC 2 summary, data flow diagram, evidence that prompt data is segregated or not used for training)?

We'd like short explicit answers we can attach to our procurement packet. If it helps, a short cover note we can quote would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sam Kim
Security & Privacy Lead
Cedar Health

--

From: logan.wright@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire: data retention & training clarifications

Sam —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then attachments and a few clarifying notes below.

1) Prompt/log retention: Default retention for API request/response telemetry is 30 days for troubleshooting and system improvement (ephemeral logs). Customers on a paid Dedicated or Private plan can opt into an account policy for 0-day retention (immediate delete) or longer windows as needed. Exportable logs for billing/usage are available via the Console; those exports are customer-controlled.

2) Training on customer data: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts, completions, or files to train our public models unless the customer explicitly signs a Data Use Agreement (DUA) that opts them in. We may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service quality metrics; that telemetry does not contain prompt-level content. For customers on Hosted API, the default is no training without opt-in.

3) Evidence: attached — filled SIG sheet, a simplified data flow diagram, and our most recent SOC 2 report (redacted where appropriate). If you need vendor-signed language for procurement, the DUA template is attached.

Notes and links (quick):
- Opt-out flow: customers can set the "Data Use" toggle in Console > Account > Data Settings, or we can apply a tenant-level policy for Dedicated/Private during provisioning.
- Ephemeral logs: used only for crash/debug traces, autoscaling diagnostics, and abuse detection; access is restricted via role-based permissions and logged.
- Retention exceptions: support snapshots for ongoing investigations can be retained longer with explicit customer approval.

I attached the SIG XLSX with cell-level responses so your team can paste answers into your procurement packet. If you'd like an official cover letter from our legal team, Marissa (cc'd) can provide that. Vivek (cc'd) can add any operational details for Dedicated/Private if you plan to host in a VPC.

Best,

— Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

If easier we can schedule a 30-minute call next week.

Sam

Sam —

Answering each point explicitly for your procurement language. You can copy/paste these into the SIG cover note.

1) Reconstruction risk: We confirm that aggregated telemetry is numeric and derived metrics (e.g., token distribution, latency buckets, error rates). Aggregation and deterministic hashing are applied such that prompt text cannot be reconstructed. Our data pipeline strips prompt payloads from metric buckets used for product analytics. We are happy to have our engineering team review a small sample of the aggregation process under an NDA if you require deeper assurance.

2) Per-project retention: For Hosted customers, retention is configurable at the project level via Console and API (Account > Projects > Data Settings). Default is account-level 30 days but you can set a per-project policy to 0 days or 7/14/30/90 days. Dedicated/Private installs can enforce tenant-level retention policies during provisioning.

3) DUA terms: Redwood can agree to a fixed-term DUA clause that prohibits use of Cedar prompts or outputs for model training for a negotiated term (e.g., 3 years) or in perpetuity with the right to revisit by mutual agreement. Our legal team typically prefers fixed terms, but Marissa can run an in-perpetuity request by Legal — we attached a draft DUA to speed review.

Additional operational controls we enforce:
- Access controls: prompt content is logically segregated; access requires a role with 'logs_view' permission.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS available for Private deployments; Hosted offers managed KMS with optional customer-managed keys on enterprise plans.
- Audit trails: every read of request/response data is logged and retained per your audit window (configurable).

Next steps:
- If you want a vendor-signed statement, Marissa will prepare a short cover letter and we can route a DUA for signature (DocuSign).
- If Cedar wants per-project 0-day retention on Hosted, we can create a temporary policy and provide a confirmation screenshot for procurement.

Would you like a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT to finalize? If yes, I can include our Security PM (Vivek) and Legal (Marissa).

Regards,
— Logan Wright
